title: Quasi-coherence of the tensor pushout algebra
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Put $A=f_*\mathcal O_U$, let $r_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_U$ be the structure map and $t_0:f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to f^{-1}A$ the inverse image of $\mathcal O_X\to A$. For any pushout square of commutative ring sheaves with legs $b:\mathcal O_U\to B$ and $t:f^{-1}A\to B$, the underlying $\mathcal O_U$-module of the algebra $(B,b)$ is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf, pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SB (lemma-affine-equivalence-modules), construction of h and elucidation

proof.text: Let G be the rank-one A-module. Its restriction along the structure map rho is the ordinary scheme-module pushforward of the rank-one O_U-module. An affine morphism is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. Apply qcqs pushforward quasi-coherence to obtain quasi-coherence of this restricted G.

The chosen tensor-pullback adjunction and the ordinary pullback adjunction have the same right adjoint. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies their left adjoints. Ordinary pullback preserves quasi-coherence, so tensor pullback of the restricted G is quasi-coherent.

Apply affine_module_tensor_baseChange to the supplied pushout. Its functor P, object equality and natural isomorphism kappa identify the underlying O_U-module of P(G) with tensor pullback of the restricted G, so P(G) is quasi-coherent after restriction along b.

Inverse image carries the rank-one A-module to the rank-one inverse-image A-module: its adjunction identifies morphisms out of the first module with compatible sections of the pushed-forward target, while the rank-one universal property identifies morphisms out of the second with compatible sections of the target. These section sets are naturally bijective since the opens preimage functor is final, and its opposite is initial (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Topology.Category.TopCat.Opens; Mathlib Functor.bijective_sectionsPrecomp). Naturality yields inverse morphisms by evaluating the Hom equivalences at identities. The same argument with the change-of-rings adjunction gives extension of a rank-one module as the target rank-one module, since scalar restriction leaves compatible sections unchanged. Both comparisons are proved as private helpers in Lean, with no new deferred theorem.

Transport the inverse-image rank-one isomorphism through the change-of-rings functor, using its recorded object equalities. Compose it with the scalar-extension rank-one isomorphism and the object equality for P(G). Restriction along b then gives an O_U-module isomorphism from restricted P(G) to the underlying module of (B,b). Transfer the quasi-coherence already established in step 3 along this isomorphism. All arguments apply to zero rings and empty spaces.

proof_origin.note: Compiling proof of Stacks 01SB tensor construction, using the existing pushout base-change comparison at the rank-one algebra module. Rank-one inverse-image and scalar-extension identifications are proved from their adjunctions; no new sorry.
